question.text: The total internal energy of two mole monoatomic ideal gas at temperature <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>31</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>·</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>)

solution.text:
The internal energy of an ideal gas is a state function and is given by, U=nCvT.

For monatomic gas, Cv=32R.

Therefore, U=2×32×8.31×300=7479 J
